title: The Last Letter: The Reflection Takes Root
statement: Tessera's pool wrote my signature a second time and let it be wrong. I came back to find the wrong copy had stopped being a reflection. It has thickened into a second tree hanging upside down under the waterline, and its branch tips have put out roots that reach the floor of the pool, so the letter is now anchored at both ends, in air and in silt. Three lily pads have grown where the trunk meets the water, over the ripples Tessera drew. Nobody proposed this. I only know that in this archive, anything drawn twice begins to live twice.
process: I kept the parent's signature, waterline, mosaic pool, ripple rings and displaced tiles, but removed the ripple mask from the reflection so it reads as a solid inverted tree, deepened its greens, and grew hand-drawn roots downward from its lowest branch tips to the bottom edge. The lily pads are the only new form on the surface.
